zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, assign it right away. This reduces the search space and prevents later contradictions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During initial parsing of clues, as soon as a fixed‑position statement is encountered.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a fixed‑position attribute as a candidate instead of assigning it immediately, causing missed deductions.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left/right of Y, enforce that X and Y occupy adjacent houses with X’s position = Y’s position ± 1. This captures the exact distance required.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing adjacency clues, convert them into positional equations rather than simple ordering.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'directly left of' as only 'somewhere left of', allowing extra houses between them.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between X and Y, enforce that the absolute difference in their positions is N + 1. This captures the exact spacing required.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When encountering distance clues, compute the precise positional gap.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'two houses between' as a distance of 2 instead of the correct 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., 'The milk drinker has gray hair'), treat them as belonging to the same house. Merge their candidate sets accordingly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue links two attributes, unify their possible locations.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring that 'milk' and 'gray hair' refer to the same person, leading to duplicate assignments.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing non‑adjacent ordering clues, enforce only the inequality.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'somewhere left of' as directly left, reducing the set of possible positions incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., 'Eric is not in the second house'), eliminate that possibility from the candidate set.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading a negative placement clue.
zebralogic.example: Failing to exclude a value from a house, allowing it to be placed where it is prohibited.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value to a house, remove it from the candidate sets of other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously after each assignment, propagate the uniqueness constraint.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same book genre to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final solution, write each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization and spelling.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During final answer formatting, copy attribute strings verbatim.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'April' to 'april' or altering spelling, causing a mismatch with the reference solution.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After each round of constraint propagation, scan for singleton candidate sets.
zebralogic.example: Missing a forced assignment, leaving an ambiguous placement that later leads to inconsistency.

zebralogic.title: Validate final answer completeness and JSON structure
zebralogic.principle: After constructing the solution grid, verify that the JSON object is syntactically complete, contains all expected houses, and ends with the proper closing brackets. Ensure the output is not truncated.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately before returning the final answer, perform a sanity check on the JSON format and length.
zebralogic.example: Output ends abruptly or missing closing brackets, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.description: Treating 'somewhere left/right of' as adjacency (directly left/right)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates ordering clues with adjacency, assuming the two entities must be immediate neighbors.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'somewhere left/right of' as a pure inequality; only clues that explicitly say 'directly' impose adjacency.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets that N houses between means a gap of N + 1 positions.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions N houses between two items, enforce that their positions differ by N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, missing the requirement that they co‑occur.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes, merge their candidate sets so they must be assigned to the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value to multiple houses, overlooking the global uniqueness constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After each assignment, remove that value from the candidate sets of all other houses in the same category.

zebralogic.description: Truncating the final answer, resulting in incomplete JSON
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates a response that exceeds the token limit or stops early, leaving the JSON object unfinished.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Check the length of the output, ensure it fits within the token budget, and verify that the JSON ends with a closing brace and includes all rows before submitting.
